curriculum_level: UNDERGRADUATE & RESIDENCY CLINICAL SKILLS TEACHING POSTER · CARDIORENAL MODULE
title: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure: Pathophysiology, Pharmacology & OSCE Guide
learning_objective: Integrate Frank-Starling hemodynamics, bedside Forrester perfusion-congestion profiling, diuretic pharmacology, and structured cardiovascular OSCE examination.

physiology_points.explanation: Falling cardiac output triggers sympathetic surge + RAAS + AVP release, elevating preload and systemic vascular resistance.
LVEDP > 18 mmHg transmits backward to pulmonary capillaries, driving interstitial and alveolar transudation.
Elevated central venous pressure reduces transrenal perfusion gradient, lowering eGFR independent of forward output.
Overstretched sarcomeres operate on flat ventricular curve where vasodilator afterload reduction restores stroke volume.

diagnostic_algorithm.pivot_test: Bedside Perfusion & Congestion Profile + BNP + Lung POCUS

branches.action: IV loop diuretic + vasodilator if SBP > 110 mmHg; monitor urine output
Assess cardiogenic shock; cautious inotrope/vasopressor + ICU invasive monitoring

matrix.title: 3. HIGH-YIELD HEART FAILURE PHARMACOLOGY MATRIX
rows: Inhibits thick ascending limb NKCC2 cotransporter
Endothelial NO -> cGMP venodilation & afterload drop
All-EF HF hospitalization & CV death reduction

osce_checklist: Position patient at 45 degrees; inspect respiratory rate, accessory muscle use, and peripheral cyanosis.
Measure Jugular Venous Pressure (JVP) height above sternal angle with tangential illumination.
Palpate apex beat (5th ICS MCL vs laterally displaced/thrusting) and parasternal RV heave.
Auscultate S3 gallop (bell at apex in left lateral decubitus) and bibasilar inspiratory crackles.
Assess dependent sacral/pretibial pitting edema and tender congestive hepatomegaly.
red_flags: SBP < 90 mmHg with cool mottled extremities, oliguria (<0.5 mL/kg/h), or rising lactate (cardiogenic shock).
SpO2 < 90% refractory to supplemental O2 requiring immediate CPAP/BiPAP ventilatory support.
Never initiate beta-blockers acutely during uncompensated pulmonary edema or low-output shock.
STEMI / acute mechanical valve or papillary muscle rupture on urgent 12-lead ECG & echo.
